question: Hádanka: Vznikol som z chyby. Chemik chcel vyrobiť čo najsilnejšiu látku na spájanie vecí, no vyšla mu taká slabá, že ma môžete odlúpiť a prichytiť znova. Dnes visím na monitoroch a chladničkách. Čo som?
source_excerpt: Working at 3M in 1968, Silver was trying to make a strong aerospace adhesive. He accidentally made the exact opposite: a weak adhesive.

extra.why_interesting: Players see sticky notes as a deliberate office product. The twist is that they exist only because an experiment failed, and the failure turned out to be the useful part.
extra.verification_notes: Post-it adhesive was invented accidentally by 3M chemist Spencer Silver in 1968 while trying to make a strong adhesive; riddle matches (https://www.todayifoundout.com/?p=5963).

explanation: Slabé lepidlo roky ležalo nevyužité, kým si ho kolega nenatrel na záložky do spevníka, aby mu v kostole nevypadávali. Z nepodareného pokusu sa tak stal jeden z najznámejších kancelárskych výrobkov.

question: Čo sa stane, keď stojíte pri zapnutom radarovom zariadení s čokoládou vo vrecku? Jednému americkému inžinierovi sa roztopila a z toho maléru vznikol spotrebič, ktorý máte asi aj vy v kuchyni. Ktorý?
source_excerpt: according to legend, a candy bar melted in his pocket

extra.why_interesting: The scenario sounds like a small lab mishap. Players can reason from 'radar waves melted chocolate' to the appliance they use every day, and it is fun to learn the microwave started as a ruined snack.
extra.verification_notes: Percy Spencer (Raytheon engineer) noticed a candy/chocolate bar melting near a magnetron, leading to the microwave oven; the story is legend-based but is the standard accepted account (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percy_Spencer).

explanation: Rovnaké vlny, aké vysielal radar, rozkmitali molekuly v čokoláde a zohriali ju. Inžinier hneď skúsil aj kukuricu a tá mu začala praskať na pukance.

question: Pravda alebo nepravda: Bublinková fólia, ktorú všetci tak radi praskáme, mala pôvodne slúžiť ako tapeta na steny.

extra.why_interesting: The claim sounds too silly to be true, so players lean towards 'Nepravda'. The truth is that the product failed at its original purpose and became famous for a different one.
extra.verification_notes: Bubble Wrap was created in 1957 by Fielding and Chavannes as textured wallpaper, and only later repurposed for packaging (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubble_Wrap_(brand)).

explanation: Vynálezcovia zlepili dva sprchové závesy a chceli predávať moderné vzorkované tapety, no nikto o ne nestál. Zachránilo ich až balenie krehkých vecí, najmä počítačov.

question: Trabant, ktorý kedysi hrkotal aj po slovenských cestách, mal karosériu, ktorá nikdy nezhrdzavela. Z čoho bola vyrobená?
source_excerpt: The body panels were made of duroplast, a hard plastic made from recycled cotton waste from the Soviet Union and phenol resins from the East German dye industry.

extra.why_interesting: Many Slovaks remember Trabants on Czechoslovak roads, so they have a real path to the answer. The 'never rusted' hint turns a joke about a bad car into a small puzzle.
extra.verification_notes: Trabant body panels were Duroplast, a cotton-reinforced resin plastic that doesn't rust, so 'plast' is correct (the steel frame could rust, a minor caveat); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trabant

explanation: Bol to duroplast, teda tvrdená živica vystužená bavlnenými vláknami, lebo oceľového plechu bolo vo východnom Nemecku málo. Nehrdzavel, no pri nehode sa namiesto pokrčenia rád roztrieštil.
